theme: कृपा और परम वचन / Grace and the supreme teaching
context: Krishna begins a further teaching, inviting Arjuna to listen for his welfare. Arjuna's request for a detailed account of Krishna's divine glories comes later, in verses 10.16–18. Here, Krishna presents his words as a caring instruction, not as a response to that later request.
contextHindi: कृष्ण आगे की शिक्षा देते हुए अर्जुन से अपने कल्याण के लिए सुनने को कहते हैं। कृष्ण की दिव्य विभूतियों का विस्तार बताने का अनुरोध अर्जुन बाद में, 10.16–18 में करता है। यहाँ कृष्ण अपने वचनों को अर्जुन के हित के लिए दी गई शिक्षा बताते हैं।
sanskritDevanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
भूय एव महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः |
यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ||१०-१||
transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca .
bhūya eva mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ .
yatte.ahaṃ prīyamāṇāya vakṣyāmi hitakāmyayā ||10-1||

wordByWord.meaning: supreme word, highest teaching; उच्चतम संदेश
to one who is cherished, to one who is beloved; जिसे भगवान प्रसन्न और प्रिय मानते हैं
for welfare, for benefit, out of desire for your good; तुम्हारे कल्याण के लिए

spokenHindi: इस श्लोक में कृष्ण अर्जुन से फिर सुनने को कहते हैं। ‘भूय एव महाबाहो’ का अर्थ है, ‘फिर से, हे महाबाहु।’ फिर वे कहते हैं, ‘मेरा परम वचन सुनो।’ ‘परमं वचः’ का अर्थ है मेरा श्रेष्ठ वचन या श्रेष्ठ उपदेश। यह कृष्ण के लिए कोई नाम नहीं है। वे कहते हैं कि वे यह बात अर्जुन से उसके कल्याण की इच्छा से कहेंगे। ‘हितकाम्यया’ का अर्थ है हित चाहकर या कल्याण के लिए। इस श्लोक में कृष्ण आगे की शिक्षा देने की बात कहते हैं। अर्जुन ने अभी यहाँ दिव्य विभूतियों का विस्तार नहीं माँगा है; वह अनुरोध आगे, 10.16–18 में आता है। इसलिए इस श्लोक को उसी क्रम में समझना चाहिए। कृष्ण अर्जुन को ध्यान से सुनने का निमंत्रण देते हैं और अपने वचन का उद्देश्य बताते हैं: अर्जुन का हित। यहाँ इतना ही स्पष्ट है कि शिक्षा फिर से कही जा रही है और वह कल्याण के लिए है।
clearEnglish: Krishna invites Arjuna to listen again to his supreme word, which he will speak out of a wish for Arjuna's welfare. The verse places the teaching within a personal relation: Arjuna is cherished, and the stated purpose is his good. The word supreme describes the teaching; it is not a separate name for Krishna. In the supplied commentary, Swami Sivananda adds that Krishna comes forward to encourage Arjuna without a request having been made. That is the commentator's account of the scene, and Arjuna's explicit request for divine manifestations occurs later. A broader modern inference is that guidance can be received more readily when care accompanies clarity. This teaching-and-learning application should be distinguished from the verse's literal statement, which does not present a general psychological theory or promise healing. One can listen attentively to a useful suggestion while still evaluating its content. Receptivity and careful judgment can therefore work together in our application.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse states that Krishna offers a supreme teaching and does so for Arjuna's welfare. The teaching is framed as compassion, not as an imposed command.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A sincere learner often does not need more argument; what is needed is a steadying relationship with the truth. The verse suggests that spiritual guidance works best when it meets the student’s suffering without contempt.

interpretationPerspectives.label: COMMENTARY
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The Divine Life Society commentary notes that the all-compassionate Lord encourages and cheered Arjuna by giving instruction Himself, without any request from Arjuna. This clarifies the emotional tone of the teaching: it is restorative and gracious.

practicalApplication.label: Listening without defense
practicalApplication.text: When you feel confused or emotionally flooded, pause and listen to one piece of guidance without immediately arguing with it. Let the teaching land before you judge it.

practicalApplication.label: Compassionate guidance
practicalApplication.text: If you help someone in pain, speak with clarity and care; a person in distress often needs steadiness more than a lecture.

reflectionQuestion: When a difficult truth is offered with compassion, how much more open are you to hearing it without immediately defending yourself?
reflectionQuestionHindi: जब कठिन सत्य को करुणा के साथ दिया जाए, तो क्या आप उसे बिना तुरंत अपने बचाव के सुना अधिक खुले मन से स्वीकार करते हैं?
